newsitem.title: FRANCE: New Nouvelles Frontieres airline to carry cargo.
newsitem.headline: New Nouvelles Frontieres airline to carry cargo.

text.p: New French airline, Aerolyon has obtained permission from France's civil aviation authority to carry freight on its passenger services from Lyon to West Africa, due to start in December, a company official told Reuters.

Aerolyon is controlled by Nouvelles Frontieres International with a 52 percent stake and Nouvelles Frontieres Aventures (48 percent). Both are subsidiaries of the French tour operator group, Nouvelles Frontieres, he added.
The group also controls another French airline, Corsair.
"From early December, we plan to have weekly services to Dakar, Lome in Togo, Ouagadougou in Burkina-Faso and Abidjan using McDonnell Douglas DC10-30 passenger aircraft," the official said.
The carrier will operate three DC10-30 planes which can each carry around 12 tonnes of cargo per flight.
Flights are likely to route Lyon-Ouagadougou-Abidjan and Lyon-Dakar-Lome, the official said.
"We are currently negotiating with the relevant authorities to obtain ex-West Africa air cargo traffic rights to Lyon and expect a positive outcome by the end of the year," he added.
He said it was likely that Aerolyon will delegate its cargo activities to Flytrucks, a subsidiary company of Aero Cargo International, which is also cargo sales agent for Corsair.
Aerolyon also plans to ship freight on weekly passenger services betwen Lyon and French overseas territories in the Caribbean and to Reunion in the Indian ocean.
The airline's maiden flight will be from Lyon to Guadeloupe in the French West Indies on November 28. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
